title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court to the Request of the Shanghai Higher People's Court and Others on Issues concerning Judicial Review of Arbitral Awards Made by the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission and Its Former Sub-Commissions and Other Arbitration Institutions

articles.content_en:
1. Where, before the renaming of the South China Sub-Commission of CIETAC to the South China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission and the Shanghai Sub-Commission of CIETAC to the Shanghai International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission, the parties concluded an arbitration agreement stipulating that disputes shall be submitted to "China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission South China Sub-Commission" or "China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission Shanghai Sub-Commission" for arbitration, the South China Sub-Commission of CIETAC or the Shanghai Sub-Commission of CIETAC shall have jurisdiction over the case. Where a party requests the People's Court to confirm the invalidity of the arbitration agreement, to set aside or not to enforce the arbitral award on the ground that the South China Sub-Commission of CIETAC or the Shanghai Sub-Commission of CIETAC has no authority to arbitrate, the People's Court shall not support such request.
Where, after the renaming of the South China Sub-Commission of CIETAC to the South China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission and the Shanghai Sub-Commission of CIETAC to the Shanghai International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission (including the date of renaming) but before the coming into force of this Reply, the parties concluded an arbitration agreement stipulating that disputes shall be submitted to "China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission South China Sub-Commission" or "China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission Shanghai Sub-Commission" for arbitration, CIETAC shall have jurisdiction over the case. However, where the applicant applies to the South China Sub-Commission of CIETAC or the Shanghai Sub-Commission of CIETAC for arbitration, and the respondent does not raise any objection to the jurisdiction of the South China Sub-Commission of CIETAC or the Shanghai Sub-Commission of CIETAC, if a party applies to set aside or not to enforce the arbitral award after the award is made on the ground that the South China Sub-Commission of CIETAC or the Shanghai Sub-Commission of CIETAC has no authority to arbitrate, the People's Court shall not support such application.
Where, after the coming into force of this Reply (including the effective date), the parties conclude an arbitration agreement stipulating that disputes shall be submitted to "China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission South China Sub-Commission" or "China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission Shanghai Sub-Commission" for arbitration, CIETAC shall have jurisdiction over the case.

2. Where, when applying to an arbitration institution for arbitration, the applicant in an arbitration case also requests the arbitration institution to make a decision on the jurisdiction of the case, and after the arbitration institution makes a decision confirming that the arbitration agreement is valid and that it has jurisdiction over the case, the respondent files a lawsuit with the People's Court to apply for confirmation of the validity of the arbitration agreement before the first hearing of the arbitral tribunal, the People's Court shall accept the case and render a ruling. Where the applicant or the arbitration institution, based on Article 3 of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning Confirmation of the Validity of Arbitration Agreements (Fa Shi [1998] No. 27) or the second paragraph of Article 13 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Shi [2006] No. 7), asserts that the People's Court shall not accept the respondent's lawsuit, the People's Court shall not support such assertion.

3. Where, before the coming into force of this Reply, CIETAC or the South China Sub-Commission of CIETAC or the Shanghai Sub-Commission of CIETAC has accepted a case that, according to the provisions of Article 1 of this Reply, should not have been accepted by it, and a party applies to set aside or not to enforce the arbitral award after the award is made on the ground that the arbitration institution has no authority to arbitrate, the People's Court shall not support such application.

4. Where, before the coming into force of this Reply, CIETAC or the South China Sub-Commission of CIETAC or the Shanghai Sub-Commission of CIETAC has accepted the same arbitration case, and a party applies to the People's Court for confirmation of the validity of the arbitration agreement before the first hearing of the arbitral tribunal, the People's Court shall hear the case and render a ruling in accordance with the provisions of Article 1 of this Reply.
Where, before the coming into force of this Reply, CIETAC or the South China Sub-Commission of CIETAC or the Shanghai Sub-Commission of CIETAC has accepted the same arbitration case, and the party does not apply to the People's Court for confirmation of the validity of the arbitration agreement before the first hearing of the arbitral tribunal, the arbitration institution that first accepted the case shall have jurisdiction over the case.
This Reply is hereby issued.
